messages:
alex: FYI bringing Suzaku-7B (Mistral-ish) into our int4 flow and seeing weird embed/proj differences for emoji-heavy inputs. Repro below, short logs included. Any ideas? :eyes:

alex: repro:
```bash
python export_model.py --name suzaku-7b --out suzaku_fp16.onnx --dtype fp16
python quantize.py --in suzaku_fp16.onnx --out suzaku_int4.onnx --backend awq --add-permute
python run_infer.py --model suzaku_int4.onnx --prompt "I ❤️ pizza" --log-tokens
```

alex: quick logs:
```
# fp16 token ids: [11, 12879, 4, 2]
# int4 token ids: [11, 6534, 4, 2]
# embedding[0] dot diff: 0.003 -> 0.12
```

alex: looks like token id split for the heart emoji changed + large change in embedding dot causing different next-token probs. My hunch: quantizer injected a permute/reshape targeting proj axes that assumes uniform head_dim.

tanya: can you paste tokenizer config and the ONNX node list?

alex: tokenizer snippet: `normalizer: {"type":"unicode_nfkc"}, pretokenizer: {"type":"byte-level"}, special: {"emoji_policy":"char_split"}`

alex: model nodes: `embedding.weight`, `attn.q_proj`, `attn.k_proj`, `attn.v_proj`, plus `permute_proj_axes` (added during quantize).

zach: permute_proj_axes = our quant shim. It's meant to reconcile Gemma vs Mistral proj layouts. If Suzaku uses non-uniform head sizes that shim will mangle offsets. What are the head dims?

alex: hetero head dims (legacy adapter): heads = [64,64,48,48,64,48,...] so not uniform. I think the global reshape assumes head_dim = 64 everywhere.

maria: also worth noting NFKC collapses some emoji sequences, but our byte-level pretokenizer can still split on codepoint boundaries. If the permute happens before embedding lookup (or if projection order changes), the byte offsets can produce different token ids.

ci-bot: run suzaku_int4_tokenize_check failed  token mismatch. CI job: https://ci.internal/3322

tanya: can you run quantize with permute disabled (`--no-permute`) and compare both token ids and logits? That'll separate tokenizer vs weight permutation issues.

alex: did that: `--no-permute` gives same token ids as FP16 for the emoji case, but logits still differ slightly (~0.5% next-token prob RMS). So two things: (1) permute caused tokenization mismatch, (2) quant rounding changes embeddings enough to move logits for multi-codepoint inputs.

zach: action: change quantizer to emit per-head reshape+transpose when head_dims are nonuniform instead of a single batch permute. I'll draft a fix.

maria: short-term mitigation: add a tokenizer pre-hook to collapse common multi-codepoint emoji sequences to canonical single codepoint during our onboarding evals. This will reduce sensitivity and give us stable baselines.

alex: ran a small eval (50 emoji prompts): fp16 vs int4 no-permute -> exact match rate 96.8%, BLEU change 0.6. fp16 vs int4 with permute -> exact match 88.4%, BLEU drop 3.9.

tanya: when you open the PR, include the minimal repro + CI link and tag `onboard/suzaku` and `quant/permute-fix`. Also add a note to backport the per-head path to the AWQ pipeline.

zach: I'll add a model-registry audit step to flag other models with hetero head dims (so we don't hit this elsewhere).

alex: I'm going to run `transform_weights.py --emit-per-head` and post a diff of proj q/k/v axis ordering to confirm. If that matches fp16 we'll be confident.

maria: and please add a unit test for multi-codepoint emoji normalization in tokenization tests. We've tripped on this twice.

ci-bot: created ticket #4782 for tokenization unit coverage.

tanya: great. once PR is up i'll kick off a canary on Dedicated with a small traffic slice.

zach: follow-up note: after changing permute approach remember to validate K/V cache indexing offsets; per-head transforms can shift KV layout assumptions. I'll add that as a checklist item in the PR.

alex: thanks all, opening PR now. summary in PR: cause = global permute + hetero head dims + NFKC/byte-level tokenizer edge-case for multi-codepoint emoji; fixes = per-head permute/reshape path, tokenizer pre-hook collapse, CI test. :thumbsup:
